registers.name_in_paper: Danish administrative data / several administrative registers linked at the individual level via personal identification numbers
registers.role: treatment, outcomes, controls, linkage and sample frame

registers.name_in_paper: Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension (ATP), the mandated pension scheme introduced in 1964
registers.role: outcomes: hours worked (37 discrete steps per year) and, with earnings, the wage rate; also the grandparental labor supply measure

registers.name_in_paper: administrative wealth measure collected for the wealth tax that existed until 1996
registers.years: 1980-1990 (used as the average net wealth of the grandfather)

linkages: individuals linked across registers via personal identification numbers
family members and generations linked: children, their parents, and their maternal and paternal grandparents
workers linked with firms (used for the family-friendliness of the firm's management and public/private sector)

sample.universe: the full population in Denmark between 1980-2013, with additional administrative data back to 1964 for the intergenerational analysis
selection_rules: first childbirths where the parents are observed every year between five years before having a child and ten years after
hence first childbirths between 1985-2003, where the parents are known, alive, and reside in Denmark throughout the 15-year window around the birth
no restrictions on the relationship status of the parents (married, cohabiting, separated, divorced or not yet in a couple)
for the very-long-run analysis (Figure 2) and the decomposition, the balanced panel is expanded to parents having their first child at any time between 1970-2013 (unbalanced panel)
occupational rank estimated conditional on not being self-employed or an assisting spouse; the family-friendly-firm outcome conditional on being in a firm with at least 10 employees
sample.period: 1980-2013 (first births 1985-2003 in the baseline sample; grandparental labor supply 1964-1979)
sample.n_individuals: around 470,000 births (i.e. the parents of around 470,000 first children)

construction_notes: event time t = 0 is the year of the first childbirth; all years are indexed relative to it and the t = -1 dummy is omitted

regressions are run in levels rather than logs so that zeros due to nonparticipation are kept; level effects are converted into percentages by dividing by the predicted outcome absent the event dummies

hours worked come from ATP pension contributions, which are a step function of hours (four bins of weekly hours 0-8, 9-17, 18-26, 27- or four bins of monthly hours 0-38, 39-77, 78-116, 117-), giving an annual hours measure in 37 steps
the wage rate is earnings divided by the ATP hours measure; hours and wage rates are conditional on participation, earnings and participation are unconditional
the ATP hours measure is capped, so the hours penalty is understated and the wage-rate penalty overstated for a given earnings penalty
occupational rank is coded in five levels (unskilled labor, skilled labor, white-collar low, white-collar high, top manager)
family friendliness of a firm is proxied by whether the firm's management includes women with children below 15 years of age
for the sector and firm outcomes (Figure 3 panels C and D), gender-specific linear pre-trends are estimated on pre-event data and the outcome is residualised with them
grandparental relative labor supply is cumulated hours worked 1964-1979 of the grandmother minus the grandfather, converted into quintile ranks

child penalties for birth cohorts before 1981 are extrapolated: the 0-10 year penalty is held constant at the average of later cohorts and the 11-20 year penalty follows the estimated linear trend; beyond event time 20 the penalty is held at its event-time-20 level
